entries.definition: uneducated in the fundamentals of a given art or branch of learning; lacking knowledge of a specific field
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the full force of 'cannot read' on one field's basics, so a limited gap sounds total - showier scorn than *ignorant*.
examples: he is musically illiterate

entries.definition: lacking knowledge gained by study often in a particular field
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A flat report that knowledge was not gained by study, in a field or in general, with none of *ignorant*'s blame.
examples: is unstudied in Latin as he is in may other matters

entries.definition: lacking in schooling
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mild, almost taking the blame off the person: the lack is in the schooling they never had, not in their mind.
examples: an untutored genius

entries.definition: act as an informer
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes the act a role: you are not someone who spoke but an informer, and the role carries a faint stain *tell* lacks.
examples: He informed on his own brother to the police.

entries.definition: to enlarge beyond bounds or the truth
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Only says something was made bigger; the fault is in going too far, not the word, so it accuses least of the three.

entries.definition: cause someone to believe an untruth
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same planting of a false belief as *deceive*, but seen as breaking the trust that made the believing possible.

entries.definition: to enlarge beyond bounds or the truth
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain accusation of overstating - past reasonable limits or past the truth - always implying the real size is smaller.
examples: tended to romanticize and exaggerate this ‘gracious Old South’ imagery

entries.definition: morally binding or necessary
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and serious: it ties the duty to whoever it rests on, where *mandatory* states it as a general rule.
examples: it is incumbent on me to attend

entries.definition: pretentiously elegant
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Scorns the elegance as put on - the height is only for show.
examples: a high-toned restaurant

entries.definition: quick and energetic
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Crisp and practical - the pace wins approval for its efficiency alone, with none of the lightness *merry* adds.
examples: a brisk walk in the park

entries.definition: quick and energetic
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: More emphasis than description, pushing quickness toward a flat-out rush in a way *brisk* never does.
examples: traveling at a rattling rate

entries.definition: having or showing great excitement and interest
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain word: it reports the excitement and interest without judging whether they are deserved, the very thing *overenthusiastic* judges.
examples: enthusiastic crowds filled the streets
an enthusiastic response
was enthusiastic about taking ballet lessons

entries.definition: (of a contest or contestants) not fairly matched as opponents
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Of a contest or its contestants, it blames the pairing itself: these two should never have been set against each other.

entries.definition: not equal or interchangeable in value, quantity, or significance
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A flat denial, not a complaint: the two are not equal or interchangeable in value, quantity or significance.

entries.definition: having a better than even chance of success
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The only word here where the imbalance is good news: a better than even chance of success, an advantage rather than a fault.
examples: the odds-on favorite

entries.definition: not caused to be equal
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Points at what was not done - nothing has been made equal - where *unequal* judges the gap that remains.

entries.definition: indicate by marking trees with blazes
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Literal where *mark* is not: the sign is really cut into trees, so the word names its method and judges nothing.
examples: blaze a trail

entries.definition: make conspicuous or noteworthy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The only one here that lifts the thing up, making it stand out or worth noticing, where *mark* just labels it.
examples: Mr. Bingley had danced with her twice, and she had been distinguished by his sisters.
with no further attempt to distinguish Elizabeth

entries.definition: completely wanting or lacking
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Light and quietly joking - a complete lack made to sound free of blame, the opposite feeling from *destitute*.
examples: innocent of literary merit

entries.definition: nonexistent
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Treats the absence as a shortfall rather than a plain fact, which is how *absent* states it.
examples: her appetite was lacking

entries.definition: reveal unintentionally
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The teller never meant to tell: it slips out and gives them away, so the fault is the slip, not the intent.

entries.definition: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Keeps the secrecy in view - what is told was meant to be kept, so the telling counts as a breach.

entries.definition: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Strips the cover off, suggesting the thing was kept back for a reason, so telling it accuses whoever kept it.
examples: Till I can forget his father, I can never defy or expose him.
Surely there can be no occasion for exposing him so dreadfully.

entries.definition: tell anonymously
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The point is the missing name: the teller stays out of sight, and the word passes no judgement on what is told.

entries.definition: make known to the public information that was previously known only to a few people or that was meant to be kept a secret
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Treats the matter as buried, not just untold, so digging is part of the word - unlike *reveal*.

entries.definition: precisely and clearly expressed or readily observable; leaving nothing to implication
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The neutral base word here: so clear that nothing is left to work out, without praising or criticising that clarity.
examples: explicit instructions
she made her wishes explicit
explicit sexual scenes

entries.definition: implied though not directly expressed; inherent in the nature of something
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral, covering both a meaning never spelled out and one that sits in a thing's nature, where *unspoken* covers only the first.
examples: an implicit agreement not to raise the subject
there was implicit criticism in his voice
anger was implicit in the argument
the oak is implicit in the acorn

entries.definition: in the nature of something though not readily apparent
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A linking phrase, not a quality: it must name what the meaning lies in, which *inherent* and *underlying* need not.
